attributes.body_ja:
「にとって」（漢字（かんじ）では「に取（と）って」）は、意見（いけん）を言（い）うときや、ある視点（してん）や立場（たちば）から何（なに）かを話（はな）すときの表現（ひょうげん）です。この表現（ひょうげん）は、たいてい名前（なまえ）や人（ひと）を指（さ）す名詞（めいし）のあとに使（つか）われますが、普通（ふつう）の名詞（めいし）に使（つか）われることもあります。「にとって」は、「(A) から見（み）て」と同（おな）じような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「にとって」は、視点（してん）や立場（たちば）などを示（しめ）す名詞（めいし）（または名詞句（めいしく））のあとにそのまま付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。

「にとって」は、もともと動詞（どうし）の「取（と）る」からできた表現（ひょうげん）で、「(A) を取（と）る」という意味（いみ）から来（き）ています。「に」は、立場（たちば）や基準（きじゅん）などを表（あらわ）す (A) を対象（たいしょう）として示（しめ）します。

「にとって」の使（つか）い方（かた）は大（おお）きく分（わ）けて、次（つぎ）の二（ふた）つがあります。

の身（み）として - (A) 個人（こじん）の視点（してん）から、人（ひと）について述（の）べる場合（ばあい）

の立場（たちば）から見（み）て - (A) の立場（たちば）から、物事（ものごと）について述（の）べる場合（ばあい）
attributes.body:
にとって (or に取（と）って when appearing as kanji) is a structure in Japanese that is used to convey opinions, or just generally to discuss something from a particular perspective. This expression regularly appears after names/pronouns, but may also be used with regular nouns. にとって is often translated as 'to (A)', 'for (A)', or 'concerning (A)'. However, it is used in almost exactly the same way as から見（み）て 'from the perspective of (A)'.

To use にとって, simply attach it to the end of a noun (or noun phrase) that you would like to express a certain viewpoint, judgment, or opinion from.

Fun Fact

にとって comes from the verb 取（と）る 'to take'. In this way, it literally means 'to take up (A)', where (A) is the location (standpoint) being highlighted with the case marking particle に. Broadly, にとって has two main uses, these are as follows:

の身（み）として - From (A)'s standpoint. (When used about people)

の立場（たちば）から見（み）て - When looking at it from (A). (When used about things)

attributes.body: にしてみれば and にとって are similar in that both express that something is true from the perspective of a certain person or group. にしてみれば is more hypothetical, e.g. 初心者にしてみればなかなか難しい implies that one might expect something to be simple, but it's difficult from the perspective of a beginner. にとって is a more neutral 'to’ or 'from the perspective of', e.g. 私にとって宝物だ ('To me, it's a prized possession.').

first_relatable.title: にしてみれば
first_relatable.meaning: For (A), In the case of (A), From (A)'s point of view, In the eyes of (A)

attributes.body: ばあいは (often written in kanji as 場合は) and に取って (often written in kana as にとって) can overlap in some cases, but not all. For example, 私の場合は and 私にとって can both mean 'as far as I'm concerned' or 'in my case'. However, since にとって simply means 'concerning', it can't replace ばあいは for the meaning of 'in the event that', e.g. 行く場合は気をつけたほうがいい ('In the event that you go, you should be careful.').

first_relatable.title: ばあいは
first_relatable.meaning: In the event of, In the case of

attributes.body: These two phrases appear similar but are used quite differently. について means 'about (A)' or 'concerning (A)' and indicates the topic of a speech, discussion, etc., e.g. ゲームについて話す ('Speak about games'), while に取って (often written in hiragana as にとって) means 'to/for (A)' or 'as far as (A) is concerned' and is typically used to express perspective or point of view, e.g. 私にとって大切な人 ('An important person to me').

に取って (often written in kana as にとって) and にしては both involve perspective, but にとって expresses personal relevance, e.g. 子供にとっては大問題だ ('It's a big issue for a child'), while にしては shows that a certain quality or characteristic defies expectations, e.g. 子供にしてはおとなしい ('He's quiet for a child').

に取って (usually written in kana as にとって) expresses viewpoint or concern, e.g. 私にとって大切な人だ ('She's an important person to me'). において・における is a formal equivalent of で, conveying setting, context, or means, e.g. 歴史において重要な出来事だ ('It's an important event in history'). Unlike にとって, the latter can directly modify nouns in the における form, e.g. 教育における問題 ('Problems in education').

second_relatable.title: において・における
second_relatable.meaning: In, On, At, Regarding, In terms of

attributes.body: に取って (usually written in kana as にとって) indicates a perspective or viewpoint, e.g. 社会にとって必要な制度だ ('It's a necessary system for society'). にしたら also means 'for (A)', but often implies a more subjective or emotional stance, e.g. 親にしたら心配だろう ('For a parent, it must be worrying').

first_relatable.title: にしたら
first_relatable.meaning: From the point of view of

attributes.body: に取って (usually written in kana as にとって) indicates a perspective or viewpoint, e.g. 私にとって大切なことだ ('It's something important to me'). には can be used this way too, e.g. 私には分からない ('It's not understandable to me'), but also has broader uses like indicating purpose, target, or scope, e.g. 成功には努力が必要だ ('To succeed, effort is necessary').

first_relatable.title: には
first_relatable.meaning: In order to, In regard to, For

attributes.body: に取って (usually written in kana as にとって) marks relevance or effect from a certain standpoint, e.g. 学生にとって分かりにくい説明だ ('It's a hard-to-understand explanation for students'). としては expresses viewpoint based on role or identity, e.g. 留学生としては反対だ ('As an exchange student, I disagree').

first_relatable.title: としては
first_relatable.meaning: As a, For a, As for

attributes.body: に取って (usually written in kana as にとって) shows viewpoint or relevance, often translated as 'to/for (A)' or 'as far as (A) is concerned', e.g. 子供にとって有害だ ('It's harmful to children'). にかけては highlights someone's strength or skill, e.g. 歌にかけては彼が一番うまい ('When it comes to singing, he's the best').

second_relatable.title: にかけては
second_relatable.meaning: When it comes to, Regarding, Concerning
